text.p: Elder-Beerman Stores Corp said on Thursday it has filed a plan of reorganization with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court that would result in the retailer being publicly traded.

Also, Elder-Beerman said the Unsecured Trade Creditors' Committee, the Employee Profit Sharing/Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) and the common shareholders support the term sheet underlying the plan, the retailer said in a statement.
The company is continuing to negotiate with the Institutional Creditors' Committee to seek consensual support for the plan, it said.
Elder-Beerman said it has managed to return to profitability on an operating bssis, increased same-store sales, remodeled stores, recruited several key executives, and closed unprofitable operations.
Elder-Beerman's proposed reorganization provides creditors and stockholders with combinations of cash, new publicly traded common stock and warrants.
Pre-petition trade creditors, unsecured bank debt holders, insurance company debt and the employee stock ownership plan will get a combination of cash and stock.

The former common stock holders would receive a combination of common stock, plus two classes of warrants, which could result in former common stockholders owning up to six percent of the reorganized company's common stock, Elder-Beerman said.
Under the plan, postpetition lenders, landlords and administrative costs for the Chapter 11 would be fully repaid in cash, the company said.
No court date has been set for consideration of the plan.
The company said it will continue to negotiate to finalize a consensual agreement.

Elder-Beerman Stores Corp, a department store chain with 50 department stores and 68 shoe stores with fiscal 1996 revenues of $569.6 million, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on October 17, 1995.
